text: SCOPE ADDITION (round-78, Andrey): ORCHESTRATOR-SKILL DEDUPE. ~/.codeterm/skills/codeterm-orchestrator/ (machine skill folder, mem-indexed as skill_codeterm_orchestrator) duplicates the product's embedded docs/ORCHESTRATION — the canonical home for orchestration discipline is 'codeterm docs ORCHESTRATION' ONLY. Disposition: (a) diff the skill folder against docs/ORCHESTRATION; (b) GENERAL discipline content -> port anything unique into the embedded doc (via a normal lane, wiring/doc revision bump); (c) MACHINE-SPECIFIC content (the build-capacity section — the only part machines were meant to adapt) -> convert to a mem preference item (kind=preference, area=orchestration, per machine); (d) DELETE the skill folder + its mem index entry after porting (mem delete skill_codeterm_orchestrator); (e) docs/ORCHESTRATION gains a short note: machine/project deltas live in mem (kind=preference, area=orchestration) and are pulled at orchestrator start — see the auto-pull task. Same disposition-table discipline as the rest of this task: every line of the skill accounted for (ported/converted/dropped-with-reason).

CORRECTED FACTS + TARGET ARCHITECTURE (round-81, supersedes the 'sync' framing in the body — Planner error corrected by code inspection): THERE IS NO SKILL SYNC IN THE PRODUCT. provider.rs:946 contract: ~/.claude/skills and ~/.agents/skills are USER-OWNED, the product MUST NOT write there (only plugin SkillFile delivery may, different mechanism). The copies found there are UNMANAGED historical duplicates (hand-copied or by old agent sessions) — nothing updates them, hence drift and orphans. ANDREY'S TARGET (verbatim intent): provider dirs contain EXACTLY ONE codeterm-related skill — 'codeterm' — a compact pointer skill whose body says: CodeTerm's knowledge lives in 'codeterm docs' (list the doc names); if you are an orchestrator, read 'codeterm docs ORCHESTRATION'; mem/sessions/keepawake quick reference or pointers. NO codeterm-orchestrator clone anywhere — not in provider dirs, not in ~/.codeterm/skills (port unique general content to docs/ORCHESTRATION, machine build-capacity to a mem preference, then delete ALL THREE copies + the mem index). REVISED DISPOSITION: (1) delete codeterm-orchestrator from all three locations after porting; (2) rewrite the codeterm skill as the pointer skill (canonical in ~/.codeterm/skills, and REGISTER how provider copies stay current — either the pointer is stable enough to never change, or document the manual update step; do NOT build a sync — the product contract forbids it); (3) strays (check-disk-space, mac-dev-test-skill, mem-testing): disposition per original body — likely delete (test artifacts), with provenance; (4) non-codeterm personal skills (atlassian, nextcloud, loom, product-bible) are Andrey's machine skills — LEAVE THEM, out of scope; (5) the guard becomes a doctor CHECK (report orphans/drift), not a sync (which would violate the user-owned contract).

EXECUTED BY PLANNER (round-82, direct user order 'удали или перенеси'). Done by hand: (1) MOVED to canon + mem-registered: check-disk-space (real infra skill -> skill_check_disk_space), mem-testing (real A/B bench procedures -> skill_mem_testing_...); (2) DELETED: mac-dev-test-skill (unfilled scaffold, placeholders verbatim) from both provider dirs; (3) DELETED all clones from ~/.claude/skills and ~/.agents/skills — both now contain EXACTLY ONE entry: codeterm (the pointer skill, per Andrey's architecture). Canon ~/.codeterm/skills holds 9 (7 original + 2 moved). REMAINING SCOPE for this task (unchanged): rewrite the codeterm skill as the compact pointer ('knowledge lives in codeterm docs; orchestrator -> codeterm docs ORCHESTRATION'); port codeterm-orchestrator content (general -> docs/ORCHESTRATION lane, build-capacity -> mem preference) then delete it from canon + mem index; doctor check for orphans/drift. The actively-harmful part (stale orchestrator clones feeding agents) is DEAD as of now.

CORRECTION (round-83, Andrey — supersedes the 'compact pointer' framing from round-81/82): the codeterm skill STAYS THE FULL CLI REFERENCE (494 lines: env, panes/workspaces, spawning, message routing, mesh, cron, services, telegram bridge, updates, plugins, usage, sessions, keepawake, config, mem, built-in docs section). Rationale: it is the universal entry point for EVERY agent on the machine — general agents, personal assistants, one-off Claude/Codex sessions — not only orchestration roles; they all learn to drive CodeTerm from it. It ALREADY ends with 'Built-in docs (read on demand)' pointing at codeterm docs — the pointer function exists as a section, not as the whole skill. REVISED remaining scope: (1) do NOT shrink or rewrite the codeterm skill; ensure canon (~/.codeterm/skills/codeterm) is the maintained source and the single provider-dir copy matches it (the drift found earlier gets reconciled: diff, port wanted edits to canon, overwrite copies; document the manual update step since no sync exists by contract); (2) codeterm-orchestrator porting + deletion unchanged (general -> docs/ORCHESTRATION, build-capacity -> mem preference); (3) doctor orphan/drift check unchanged — it now also guards the codeterm skill copy staying equal to canon.
